description: The macro is called with a fixed list (MOT HOM TRV) and only those three score tables are unioned. Customer/line rows in claims_enriched with any other lob_code, including a differently cased or null code, never reach rpt.risk_scores. Their claims still count towards the line loss ratios.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, SUM(total_paid) AS paid FROM dw_claims_enriched WHERE lob_code IS NULL OR lob_code NOT IN ('MOT','HOM','TRV') GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code) x

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, SUM(total_paid) AS paid FROM dw_claims_enriched WHERE lob_code IS NULL OR lob_code NOT IN ('MOT','HOM','TRV') GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code) x
intended_behaviour: Score every line of business in the claims experience, with the list built from the data (e.g. select distinct lob_code into a macro variable) instead of hard-coded.
title: Hard-coded line-of-business list drops other lines

description: Points and score are built with + and *, which pass missing values through. If n_recoveries is missing (every claim has null n_recoveries), loss_ratio is missing (the line has no row in premium_band_summary because of the inner join in lob_ratio), or age_load/county_load are missing (the customer is not in dim_customer, through the left join), then points and score come out missing. The tier IF chain then sends a missing score to 'LOW'. The author clearly wanted a default for missing values (a missing age gets age_load 1.00 on line 25), but unmatched customers and missing components get no default.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ROUND((12.5*LEAST(n_claims,4) + 7.5*COALESCE(n_recoveries,0) + CASE WHEN severity >= 2 THEN 10 WHEN severity >= 1 THEN 5 ELSE 0 END + COALESCE(ROUND(5*loss_ratio)/2,0)) * COALESCE(age_load,1) * COALESCE(county_load,1), 2)),0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores WHERE score IS NULL

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ROUND((12.5*LEAST(n_claims,4) + 7.5*COALESCE(n_recoveries,0) + CASE WHEN severity >= 2 THEN 10 WHEN severity >= 1 THEN 5 ELSE 0 END + COALESCE(ROUND(5*loss_ratio)/2,0)) * COALESCE(age_load,1) * COALESCE(county_load,1), 2)),0) AS amount_affected FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores WHERE score IS NULL
intended_behaviour: Default missing components to neutral values: recoveries 0, lob_points 0, loads 1.00. Then compute a real score and tier, or flag the row explicitly instead of quietly putting it in LOW.
title: Missing inputs make the score missing and silently tier the row LOW

description: work.cust takes every row of dw.dim_customer with no filter for the current version. The dimension has version_count/_row_seq columns, which suggests it keeps history. The left join on customer_id then repeats each customer/line score row once per customer version, and ages or counties can differ between versions.

impact.query: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(n-1),0) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))*(n-1)),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(paid) AS paid FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) d

impact_query: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(n-1),0) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))*(n-1)),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, COUNT(*) AS n, MAX(paid) AS paid FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code HAVING COUNT(*) > 1) d
intended_behaviour: Join exactly one (current) customer record per customer_id, so there is one output row per customer and line.
title: Customer dimension join can multiply score rows

description: Age is int((as_of - date_of_birth)/365.25). This understates the age of people whose birthday falls on or just before the reporting date (e.g. born 2000-12-31 gives 24, not 25 at 2025-12-31). That can move them across the 25 or 70 loading boundaries.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores g WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dw_dim_customer c WHERE CAST(c.customer_id AS DOUBLE) = g.customer_id AND c.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL AND (2025 - YEAR(c.date_of_birth)) <> g.age)

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected FROM golden_rpt_risk_scores g WHERE EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM dw_dim_customer c WHERE CAST(c.customer_id AS DOUBLE) = g.customer_id AND c.date_of_birth IS NOT NULL AND (2025 - YEAR(c.date_of_birth)) <> g.age)
intended_behaviour: Use the exact completed age at the reporting date (e.g. intck('year', date_of_birth, &as_of, 'c')). At 2025-12-31 this is 2025 - year(date_of_birth).
title: Age approximated by days/365.25

description: as_of is used only for age. Claims, payments and recoveries are taken from claims_enriched whatever their loss or reported date, so claims after the reporting date add to counts, paid, severity and loss ratio.

impact.query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, SUM(total_paid) AS paid FROM dw_claims_enriched WHERE lob_code IN ('MOT','HOM','TRV') AND (loss_date > DATE'2025-12-31' OR reported_date > DATE'2025-12-31') GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code) x

impact_query: SELECT COUNT(*) AS rows_affected, COALESCE(SUM(ABS(COALESCE(paid,0))),0) AS amount_affected FROM (SELECT customer_id, lob_code, SUM(total_paid) AS paid FROM dw_claims_enriched WHERE lob_code IN ('MOT','HOM','TRV') AND (loss_date > DATE'2025-12-31' OR reported_date > DATE'2025-12-31') GROUP BY customer_id, lob_code) x
intended_behaviour: Keep only claims with loss_date (or reported_date) on or before &as_of.
title: Claims experience not limited to the reporting date
